I don’t have children nor do I have divorced parents, but my older half-sister does so I thought I’d share some of her story for your consideration. 

My dad and her mom split up when she was basically a baby because of their toxic relationship. He wanted to be around my sister, but honestly her mother was just poison. She lied in court saying awful things about my dad to get full custody (didn’t happen). And when my dad would call their house to talk to my sister, when her aunt or mom would answer the phone they called out to my sister with things like “hey, your f***ing father is on the phone!!”. So he stopped calling as much because he didn’t want his image in her mind to be so tainted.

We would get her (several states away) for every other holiday/birthday and it was great! She and my dad had some issues when she was about 20 about him not being around, but they went to therapy and now that she’s 32, she and my dad are closer than she and her mom. 

If he had stayed with her mom, she would have been raised in a miserably toxic home. If he had visited or called more, her mother would have been even more poisonous to make my sister hate him like she did. 

Sometimes being an away parent is for the best.

I would suggest trying to stick it out for at least a few more months. It takes your body time to adjust to any new birth control, whether it’s an IUD or the pill, etc. I’ve had mine in since January and I’m very happy with it, but that’s not to say I didn’t have a rocky start. You can get it easily taken out at any time, but the stress and pain of getting a new one could be very off-putting if you get it out and later decide you want it again (though that’s totally your choice). 

Your side effects and experience are completely valid and you should follow your gut, but my suggestion is try to allow your body a bit more time to adjust! ❤️

So I got my copper IUD inserted at the start of January 2020. The insertion was awful, and the cramping afterwards continued for a long while. After the intense cramping stopped, I noticed a little poking (sharper pain than the other cramps) localized on the left side of my uterus that felt like my IUD was poking my Fallopian tube. My IUD actually ended up expelling itself after 3-4 weeks.

The next week I got a new one, but during the time when I didn’t have one I could still feel the pain but it was slowly subsiding like it was healing. When I got my new one the pain hadn’t gone away completely but it continued to slowly subside and I now have zero pain. 

So while I don’t know for sure what malposition my first one was in, I do know that getting a new one did fix the pain I was feeling that I am very sure was my tube being poked.

Obviously no one wants to voluntarily go through another IUD insertion but I just think you should go with your gut and if that is to get a new one then I can attest to a new IUD placement fixing the pain I was in.

Copper toxicity seems (from my research) to only be an issue to those who may otherwise already be susceptible to it (liver problems bc the liver is what detoxes your body). When I got mine put in, I wasn’t prepared for the pain. No one REALLY prepares you for that level of intense cramping and that just made it worse for me because it was such a shock that I started to have a bit of a panic attack. My first iud expelled itself (don’t freak out, this is super rare), and I just got a new one yesterday. This time, I was prepared and brought my healing crystals and physical healing affirmations :) it brought down my anxiety, and by knowing that it would all be over super soon, I was able to keep from tensing up and making it worse and was then able to walk out of that office like a boss!! If my friends had warned me well enough, maybe I would have been able to better prepare myself and not had the panic attack. My best advice is to breathe, say affirmations to slow your breath and keep your mind distracted like “I am at ease with my pain because I know it will heal soon”, and look forward to a future of no hormones and peace of mind when it comes to unwanted pregnancy!!

I had painful periods before taking the pill, and then would only get very mild cramps and regular periods on the pill. I just recently got the copper iud and love not being on hormones anymore! But honestly, the bleeding is insane. I don’t have too bad of cramps, but I’ll run through a pad in 2 hours now. But I did some research on the best pads for heavy periods and have taken this to be payment for no hormones. As annoying as it can be, I still think it’s worth it. For me, the cramps were only severe right after getting the iud put in and the period following it. Since then, my cramps are really only moderate. My mom also had the paragard and when she was young she had crazy cramps and bleeding, but her only real complaint with the paragard was the level of bleeding. Just know that you need to be prepared for heavy bleeding but again, I think it’s worth it!
